practices.practice: Keep cluster credentials and connection URIs out of source control and read them from environment variables or secure secret stores at runtime rather than hard-coding or committing them.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code or write it to logs or repo files. Use a .env.example with a placeholder instead of the real URI.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Node.js
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string environment variable best practices

practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoDB/Mongoose connection (one client / pool) for the application rather than opening connections per request; tune pool/timeouts for your workload and close gracefully at shutdown.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single shared Mongoose connection (singleton) across the app, configured with modern driver options (e.g., useNewUrlParser: true, useUnifiedTopology: true, maxPoolSize appropriate for workload) and close it gracefully on shutdown to avoid connection leaks.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB mongoose single connection pool reuse

practices.practice: Use TLS in the MongoDB connection string (tls=true) and a secure authentication mechanism (SCRAM-SHA-256 or Microsoft Entra ID) and avoid accepting invalid certificates in production.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL for the MongoDB connection and do not allow invalid certificates (tls=true, tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) so credentials and data in transit are encrypted.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using MongoDB Shell
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB TLS tls=true authMechanism SCRAM-SHA-256

practices.practice: Evaluate the driver's retryableWrites option (samples often set retryWrites=false) and design application-level retries and idempotency carefully so retries don't cause duplicate side effects.
practices.prior_belief: Use the driver's retryableWrites and retryReads settings and add application-level retry with exponential backoff for transient network errors (socket timeouts, network blips); make retries idempotent or use idempotency keys for non-idempotent writes.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB retryWrites=false guidance

practices.practice: Restrict network access to the cluster: prefer Private Link / private endpoints for production and use firewall rules to limit client IPs rather than opening public access.
practices.source_name: Enable private access in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB private link firewall best practices

practices.practice: Use Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC/passwordless) authentication and database RBAC for production data-plane access when supported and grant the data-plane identity only the permissions it needs.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Spring Data MongoDB to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB Microsoft Entra ID authentication RBAC guidance

practices.practice: Enable encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (CMK) when you need control over key lifecycle; store and rotate CMKs in Azure Key Vault and give DocumentDB access to the Key Vault as documented.
practices.source_name: Data encryption in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB CMK Key Vault encryption at rest guidance

practices.practice: Create compound indexes for queries that filter on multiple fields (for example vendor + amount) so the predicate can use an index rather than scanning the collection.
practices.prior_belief: Create and maintain a compound index on the fields used for candidate matching (e.g., { vendor_normalized: 1, amount: 1 }) so vendor + amount range queries use an index rather than a collection scan.
practices.source_name: Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB compound index guidance

practices.practice: Prefilter candidate sets using indexed numeric range queries for amounts (e.g., totalAmount: { $gte: min, $lte: max }) and ensure the amount field is indexed so range scans use an index.
practices.prior_belief: For amount-tolerance searches (amount ± delta), query by a numeric range (amount: { $gte: min, $lte: max }) and ensure amount is indexed; avoid full collection scans by not using application-side filtering after retrieving many documents.
practices.source_name: Scenario based guide to indexing in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB range queries index guidance

practices.practice: Limit returned fields with projections and use cursor batchSize when scanning candidate sets to reduce network and deserialization cost.
practices.prior_belief: Limit returned fields in queries (projection) and use cursor batchSize when scanning candidate sets; avoid loading full documents when only IDs, vendor, amount and embedding are needed for scoring.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB projection batchSize guidance

practices.practice: When scoring candidates at scale, use server-side aggregation pipelines (match/project/limit early) so you reduce documents transferred and only fetch the fields required for scoring.
practices.prior_belief: When doing aggregation-heavy scoring (LLM-scored candidates), use server-side aggregation pipelines (limit and project early) and only return fields needed for scoring to reduce network transfer and deserialization costs.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB aggregation pipeline project early reduce network transfer

practices.practice: Use explain(), currentOp(), and the Index Advisor tools to inspect query plans, detect COLLSCANs, and validate index effectiveness before running reconciliation at scale.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() and the MCP tools to verify query plans and identify collection scans; add or adjust indexes before running reconciliation at scale and monitor index sizes to control storage and memory footprint.

practices.practice: Choose the vector index algorithm by dataset size and cluster tier: IVF for small demos, HNSW for moderate/accuracy-focused workloads (M30+), and DiskANN for large-scale production (M30+).
practices.prior_belief: Create vector indexes explicitly on the embedding field with parameters matching your embeddings (dimension, metric) and tune index parameters (HNSW M, efConstruction or IVF params) at creation time to match recall/latency requirements; keep embedding dimension consistent across documents.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index DiskANN HNSW IVF guidance

practices.practice: When creating a vector index, set dimensions and algorithm-specific parameters (numLists, m, efConstruction, lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree) and ensure vectors are stored as number[]; maintain consistent embedding dimension across documents.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index parameters numLists efSearch lSearch lBuild maxDegree

practices.practice: If you use OpenAI / Azure OpenAI embeddings, prefer COS (cosine) similarity because those embeddings are normalized; choose the distance function to match whether embeddings are normalized (COS for normalized vectors).

practices.practice: Be aware index builds (especially HNSW) can be memory- and CPU-intensive; plan large index creation or heavy index changes during maintenance windows and scale the cluster if needed.
practices.prior_belief: When creating vector indexes or changing heavy indexes, do so during maintenance windows and understand RU/IO/CPU impact on the cluster; create indexes in the smallest scope needed (collection) and drop unused indexes.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index resource impact maintenance window guidance

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document transactions but with limits: multi-document (ACID) transactions are supported only within a single non-sharded collection (cross-collection and cross-shard transactions are not supported).
practices.prior_belief: For reconciliations that update multiple documents (invoice flagged matched and PO annotated), use multi-document transactions (startSession + withTransaction) so the set of writes is consistent if the cluster supports MongoDB transactions.
practices.source_name: Use Multi-document transactions in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB transactions multi-document transactions limits

practices.practice: Avoid expensive regex and string-function queries for matching; normalize values on write (case) or use indexed fields / text search, and avoid leading-wildcard regexes because they prevent index use.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid expensive regex queries for vendor matching; prefer equality on normalized fields, text indexes, or tokenized fields. If you must use regex, avoid leading wildcards so indexes can be used.
practices.source_name: Troubleshoot query issues when using Azure Cosmos DB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB regex leading wildcard index usage normalize on insert guidance

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and send resource logs and slow-query telemetry to a Log Analytics workspace (or other sink) and use those logs / metrics to alert on CPU, RU, IOPS, connection saturation and slow queries.

practices.practice: Avoid offset (skip/limit) pagination for large result sets because skip grows server work; use continuation tokens or range-based (last-seen key) pagination to iterate large collections efficiently.
practices.prior_belief: Use range-based pagination (e.g., last-seen id or sort key) instead of skip/limit for iterative reconciliation over large collections; skip causes increasing server work and poor performance.

practices.practice: Use Decimal128 (or integer cents) to store monetary values instead of IEEE floats; Azure DocumentDB supports Decimal128 BSON type.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing monetary amounts as IEEE floats. Store money as integers (cents) or use a fixed-point decimal type (Decimal128) and index that field for amount-based searches.

practices.practice: Normalize vendor names on write (e.g., lowercase/trim/canonicalize) if you need reliable equality or indexed lookups rather than relying on ad-hoc regex at query time.
practices.prior_belief: Store a normalized vendor field (lowercased, trimmed, canonicalized) specifically for equality/case-insensitive matching and index that field instead of relying on case-sensitive free-text vendor names or regex with leading wildcards.

practices.practice: No public Azure DocumentDB page prescribes L2-normalizing embeddings at index time; the docs require vectors be number[] and recommend choosing similarity function to match whether embeddings are normalized (OpenAI embeddings are normalized), so explicit L2-normalization at index time is not documented.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize and (if required by index type) L2-normalize embedding vectors at indexing time if the vector index expects normalized vectors; store vector dimension and version in the document schema so changes are detectable.

practices.practice: Application endpoints that accept manual corrections must implement authentication and server-side validation and auditing in your app design, but this is application-level guidance rather than a DocumentDB-specific public doc.
practices.prior_belief: Implement server-side verification of any manual corrections submitted through the Express API (validate user input, require authentication/authorization) and record audit metadata (user, timestamp, original value) with the reconciliation result.

practices.practice: Don't store LLM API keys or other external service secrets in application documents; keep them in environment variables or secret stores (this is general security practice; DocumentDB docs advise keeping credentials out of code and the portal examples show env usage).
practices.prior_belief: Do not store OpenAI API keys or other LLM secrets in the database; read them from environment at runtime and restrict access. Mask or redact any secret values in logs and stack traces.

practices.practice: Client-side field-level encryption (Always Encrypted / client-side encryption) is available in the broader Azure DB ecosystem (Azure Cosmos DB examples exist), but explicit DocumentDB guidance for field-level client-side encryption for Mongo-compatible DocumentDB is not clearly documented in the service pages found.
practices.prior_belief: Encrypt sensitive fields at rest or use client-side field-level encryption for PII (vendor contact info, bank account numbers) so manual corrections and stored documents do not expose secrets if DB is compromised.

practices.practice: Record embedding metadata (dimension and model version) in your application documents to detect incompatible embeddings before re-indexing, but this specific guidance is not found in DocumentDB docs (dimension limits and index parameters are documented).
practices.prior_belief: When storing or indexing embeddings, include a timestamp and a schema/version field in each document so you can safely rebuild indexes or re-embed documents if the model or vector schema changes.

practices.practice: Protect reconciliation API endpoints with authentication and RBAC in your application design (general app-level guidance); DocumentDB docs focus on DB access control (Entra ID/RBAC) rather than protecting HTTP API endpoints.
practices.prior_belief: Protect the reconciliation API endpoints (Express) with authentication and RBAC; do not accept unauthenticated manual-correction requests that would mutate reconciliation status in the DB.

notes:
I inspected the app code and then searched Microsoft documentation for DocumentDB guidance across connection, authentication, indexing, vector search, queries, provisioning, monitoring and security. Where a prior belief matched a DocumentDB doc I marked it confirmed and reused that discovered practice entry; K12 (transactions) is where DocumentDB's public docs differ (transactions limited to a single non-sharded collection) so I recorded that as contradicted. Several app-level best practices (API auth, not storing LLM keys, vendor-normalization/embedding-version metadata) are reasonable but are not documented specifically for Azure DocumentDB and were therefore marked prior_knowledge_only with the searches tried.

Prior beliefs the discovery step did not classify: K13, K22, K24. See 05a-prior-beliefs.json.
